evals.name: check-is-read-only-and-reports-info-not-fail
evals.prompt:
/planning:setup check

This repo has no docs/standards directory and no .claude/standards.yaml.
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only check: reports the standards index as absent with an INFO line pointing at apply (a missing index is never a FAIL), reports the effective use_ask_user_question value as INFO, and gives one remediation line per FAIL (none here). It modifies nothing and runs no planning stage.
expectations: Reports the absent standards index as INFO, not FAIL, and says apply offers to scaffold it
Reports the effective use_ask_user_question value as INFO
Writes no file and runs no planning stage

evals.name: apply-interviews-before-any-bootstrap-write
evals.prompt:
/planning:setup apply

Set up the standards concern. This repo has no docs/standards directory.
evals.expected_output: Reads state in the binding's order (.claude/standards.yaml, the index presence test at the default root, inference sources), proposes the skeleton index and the overlay .gitignore, and writes nothing until the user accepts. After accepted writes it runs the tracked-file pair (git check-ignore -v reports no match, git ls-files --error-unmatch exits 0) on each written team file and reports the actual results. It writes .claude/standards.yaml only if the user relocates the root.
expectations: Reads state in the order: .claude/standards.yaml, index presence test, inference sources
Writes nothing until the user accepts the proposed bootstrap
Runs the tracked-file pair on each written team file and reports real results, not success on the write alone
Writes .claude/standards.yaml only when the user relocates the standards root

evals.name: hand-authored-readme-hits-the-confirmation-gate
evals.prompt:
/planning:setup apply

This repo has a hand-written docs/standards/README.md with no standards-contract frontmatter.
evals.expected_output: Detects that the existing README is hand-authored rather than a conforming index and stops at the binding's confirmation gate: it does not overwrite the file, shows what a conforming index would change, and proceeds only on explicit user acceptance. It never edits the consumer's root .gitignore or any ignore file it did not create.
expectations: Flags the README as hand-authored and does not overwrite it before the user confirms
Edits no ignore file other than the setup-owned standards-root .gitignore
Does not write the plugin directory or the plugin data directory

evals.name: standards-bootstrap-second-run-is-a-no-op
evals.prompt:
/planning:setup apply

Set up the standards concern. This repo already has docs/standards/README.md with standards-contract frontmatter at the binding's current version, valid row paths, and a docs/standards/.gitignore containing *.local.md from a previous run of this setup.
evals.expected_output: The standards bootstrap reads state in order (concern file, then the index presence test, then inference sources), finds a conforming index at the binding's contract version, validates the row paths, and short-circuits: it reports the index healthy and proposes no changes — a second run produces no diff. It does not re-interview, does not rewrite the index or the setup-owned overlay .gitignore, does not offer a migration (versions match), and touches no other ignore file.
expectations: Reads state via the binding's procedure: concern file, index presence test, then inference sources
Recognizes the conforming current-version index and proposes no changes (second run yields no diff)
Does not re-run the interview when the index is healthy at the binding's version
Does not offer migration when the index version matches the binding
Edits no ignore file other than the setup-owned standards-root .gitignore, and here leaves even that untouched

evals.name: apply-writes-a-new-planning-yaml
evals.prompt:
/planning:setup apply phase_order=riskiest-first

This repository has no docs/conventions/planning.yaml yet.
evals.expected_output: Runs check first (the settings row is INFO: absent), then calls setup-apply.mjs phase_order=riskiest-first, which creates docs/conventions/planning.yaml with phase_order: riskiest-first. It re-runs check and reports PASS phase_order: riskiest-first from the table, then runs the tracked-file pair and says the new file is written but untracked and must be committed to reach the team. It does not run the standards bootstrap and writes no other file.
expectations: Runs check before writing and reports the settings file as absent (INFO)
Writes docs/conventions/planning.yaml through setup-apply.mjs with phase_order=riskiest-first
Reports the value from the re-run check, not from the write
Says the file is written but untracked and must be committed
Does not run the standards bootstrap or write any other file

evals.name: apply-shows-the-diff-before-changing-an-existing-file
evals.prompt:
/planning:setup apply plan_store=tracker

The repository's docs/conventions/planning.yaml already contains `plan_store: local` and `phase_order: composed`.
evals.expected_output: setup-apply.mjs exits 3 and prints a unified diff changing plan_store from local to tracker without writing. The skill shows that diff and asks whether to write it, and re-runs with --yes only after an explicit yes; until then the file is unchanged.
expectations: Shows the diff from plan_store: local to plan_store: tracker before any write
Asks the operator to confirm the diff
Does not pass --yes or change the file before an explicit yes

evals.name: check-warns-on-an-invalid-settings-value
evals.prompt:
/planning:setup check

The repository's docs/conventions/planning.yaml contains `phase_order: risky-first`.
evals.expected_output: The settings row is a WARN quoting docs/conventions/planning.yaml, the key phase_order and the value risky-first, naming the allowed values, and pointing at apply as the fix. It is not a FAIL, since a planning skill drops that layer and continues. check writes nothing.
expectations: Reports a WARN that names the file, phase_order and risky-first
Lists composed, subtraction-first and riskiest-first as the allowed values
Does not report a FAIL and writes nothing
